title: Body
hook: the body as a temple: sleep, food, movement
tomorrow: Jesus gives thanks for five loaves. why thank God for so little?

segments.voice: Yesterday, screens: the eye steers the whole person. Your line was guard your attention. Today, the body doing the looking.
screen: `GUARD YOUR ATTENTION.` → `THE BODY DOING THE LOOKING.`

segments.voice: Running on almost no sleep gets worn like a badge sometimes. The prophet Elijah hits the bottom of that. Worn out and running for his life, he sits under a juniper tree in the wilderness and asks to die: “It is enough; now, O LORD, take away my life.” What comes next is not a lecture. He falls asleep. An angel touches him and says, “Arise and eat.” Bread, water, more sleep, more food. Only then, the journey.
screen: `NO SLEEP, WORN LIKE A BADGE.` → `ELIJAH: IT IS ENOUGH.` → `ARISE AND EAT.`

segments.voice: So, one question: is caring for the body holy, or just maintenance? Paul answers it in a letter to Corinth: “What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own?” A temple: a place where God is honored. Sleep, food and movement become ways of keeping that place. A psalm says it with wonder: “I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made.” Now a neighbor who says something close. In an old Jewish midrash, the sage Hillel is walking with his students and tells them he's off to do a mitzvah, a commanded good deed. Which one? Bathing. If the keepers of a king's statues wash them, how much more a person, since the Torah says, in the old Jewish translation, “for in the image of God made He man.” Shared: caring for the body is not vanity; it's honoring what God made. One honest difference. Hillel's reason is the image of God, which Christians read in Genesis too. Paul adds a Christian claim, the Holy Spirit dwelling within, a body “bought with a price.” And if Elijah's low place is ever yours, reach out: call or text 988 in the US, or local emergency help.
screen: `A TEMPLE OF THE HOLY GHOST.` · `FEARFULLY AND WONDERFULLY MADE.` · `HILLEL'S BATH: A GOOD DEED.` · `SHARED IMAGE, DIFFERENT REASON.` · then, large: `CARE FOR THE TEMPLE.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and travel slowly through your body, from your feet up to your forehead. Notice where it's tired, without fixing anything yet. Before you open your eyes, choose tonight's bedtime, a little earlier than usual.
Body. Not a shell to drag around, but a temple to keep: slept, fed and moved with care.
Keep this one: care for the temple, starting with an earlier bedtime tonight. Day 1728, kept.

howItsDone: Christians care for the body in different ways: grace before meals, Sunday rest, fasting in some seasons and feasting in others; some churches anoint the sick with oil and pray for healing.

notes: New v3 script (no earlier draft). v3 wisdom shape with the unity thread: one question (is caring for the body holy?), the Christian answer (1 Corinthians 6:19–20; Psalm 139:14), a neighbor in its own words and source (Hillel's bathhouse teaching, Leviticus Rabbah 34:3, citing Genesis 9:6, quoted from JPS 1917), one shared thing (care of the body as honoring what God made) and one honest difference (Paul's claim of the indwelling Holy Spirit and a body 'bought with a price', which is specifically Christian). Hillel story paraphrased: in Leviticus Rabbah 34:3 Hillel, leaving his students, says he is going to perform a mitzvah; asked which, he says bathing in the bathhouse, reasoning from the keepers of kings' statues who wash them. A Jewish reviewer should confirm the paraphrase and the citation (some editions number it 34:3).
